observation_summary: The method NumberUtils.createNumber incorrectly returned null when encountering a string starting with '--', which violated the expected behavior of throwing a NumberFormatException. The fix involved removing the incorrect null-returning check and adding a proper validation check that throws a NumberFormatException when such an invalid input is detected.
reasoning_summary: The bug was caused by an incorrect conditional check that returned null instead of throwing an exception. The fix involved removing the incorrect logic and adding a proper validation guard (a check) that throws a NumberFormatException, which is the standard way to handle invalid input in this context. This fits the definition of 'Checking' as it involves correcting predicate logic and validation of input data.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows the removal of 'if (str.startsWith("--")) { return null; }' from the beginning of the method.
The fix diff shows the addition of 'if (str.trim().startsWith("--")) { throw new NumberFormatException(...); }' in the BigDecimal creation logic.
The bug report states that returning null is contrary to the Javadoc and expected behavior.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not about changing the computational steps of number parsing, but rather about enforcing a validation rule (guard) on the input string.
The issue is not about an incorrect value being assigned, but about the control flow logic failing to validate the input correctly.
